audit.primary_source_citation: Bruno A, Focaccetti C, Pagani A, Imperatori AS, Spagnoletti M, Rotolo N, Cantelmo AR, Franzi F, Capella C, Ferlazzo G, Mortara L, Albini A, Noonan DM. "The proangiogenic phenotype of natural killer cells in patients with non-small cell lung cancer." Neoplasia. 2013 Feb;15(2):133-142. doi:10.1593/neo.121758. PMID 23441128; PMCID PMC3579316. UPSTREAM CONVERSION SOURCE (cited by Bruno as ref 24 for the phenotype-switch step): Keskin DB, Allan DS, Rybalov B, Andzelm MM, Stern JN, Kopcow HD, Koopman LA, Strominger JL. "TGFbeta promotes conversion of CD16+ peripheral blood NK cells into CD16- NK cells with similarities to decidual NK cells." PNAS. 2007;104(9):3378-3383. PMID 17360654; PMCID PMC1805591.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Full text obtained, but NOT via the standard route: PMC3579316 is not in the PMC Open Access subset (oa.fcgi returns "idIsNotOpenAccess") and EuropePMC fullTextXML returns HTTP 404, so `lit.py methods 23441128` reported STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY. Verbatim text was recovered by direct curl of the PMC article HTML and archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC3579316_fulltext.txt (60 kB). Keskin 2007 recovered the same way: /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC1805591_fulltext.txt. Two WebFetch passes over the same PMC page returned mutually inconsistent paraphrases (one said "3 weeks", one said "7 days"); the raw text shows the paper itself is internally inconsistent on this point, so all quotes below are from the raw HTML, not from any model paraphrase.
audit.species: Human (Homo sapiens) throughout the primary source: NSCLC surgical patients, bullectomy patients, healthy buffy-coat/blood donors. No animal work in the primary source. (Mouse appears only in the 2026 downstream galunisertib PDAC paper, and there only as an infiltration/abundance readout.)
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, at a single cross-sectional timepoint (the moment of surgical resection, no follow-up sampling), the percentage of CD3-CD56+CD16- vs CD56+CD16+ NK cells and their intracellular VEGF, PlGF, IL-8/CXCL8 and IFN-gamma content after PMA/ionomycin restimulation were measured by multicolour flow cytometry in paired tumour, macroscopically normal adjacent lung, and peripheral blood from 31 NSCLC patients, compared against 10 bullectomy patients and 12 healthy blood donors. Supernatants from FACS-sorted CD56+CD16- NK cells were assayed for HUVEC chemotaxis and Matrigel capillary-like structure formation in vitro. Separately, in vitro, VEGF/PlGF expression was measured by flow cytometry within a CD56+CD16- gate in BULK (unsorted, negatively-enriched "Total") healthy-donor buffy-coat NK cells after 3 weeks of culture in IL-2 (100 U/ml) + SCF (20 ng/ml) with or without TGF-beta1 at 2, 5 or 10 ng/ml. No individual cell, and no donor's cells, were ever followed over time from a CD16+ to a CD16- state in this paper: the CD56bright-CD16- proportion shift (approx. 30% to approx. 70%) is reported as "(data not shown)" and explicitly attributed to prior work. The paper therefore contains NO original data on conversion; it measures abundance and cytokine content at one timepoint.
audit.n: 31 NSCLC patients (median age 71, range 44-79; paired tumour + adjacent lung + peripheral blood); 10 bullectomy control patients (median age 27, range 16-69; blood + macroscopically normal lung); 12 healthy peripheral-blood donors for the blood comparison (8 with median age 54, range 44-68, plus 4 anonymous donors). For the TGF-beta1 in vitro polarization experiment (Figure 6), the number of buffy-coat donors is NOT REPORTED anywhere in the methods, results or figure legend; the paper contains no "n =" statement at all and no statement of independent-experiment replicates.
audit.n_unit: human subjects (patients and blood donors); the in vitro TGF-beta1 arm has no reported donor n
audit.controls: Human arm: internal paired control of macroscopically normal adjacent lung from the same 31 patients; external control of 10 bullectomy patients (blood + normal lung) and 12 healthy blood donors. MAJOR CONTROL DEFECT: the bullectomy control group has median age 27 (range 16-69) against patient median 71 (range 44-79) — a roughly 44-year median gap in a comparison whose entire readout is NK subset proportion, which is age-dependent; the healthy blood donors (median 54) are also younger. No smoking-status matching is reported for controls despite 90% of patients being current/former smokers. In vitro arm: only "same medium without TGF-beta1" as a vehicle control. There is NO sorted starting population (cells were cultured as "Total NK"), NO viability/apoptosis or proliferation (CFSE/Ki67) accounting, NO time course, NO cell-tracking, NO adoptive transfer, NO lineage tracing or genetic fate mapping, and no statistical n. Statistics were "two-tailed t tests ... for comparison of paired data sets and quartile localization for population distribution", with no correction for multiple comparisons across four cytokines x three compartments x two histologies.
audit.methods_quote: METHODS (TGF-beta1 arm, verbatim): "We evaluated cytokine production (VEGF, PlGF, IL-8, and IFN-gamma) after TGFbeta1 stimulation on peripheral blood NK cells isolated from buffy coats of healthy donors by negative selection NK cell enrichment as above. Total NK cells were cultured in RPMI 1640 (1 x 10^6/ml) supplemented with FBS, IL-2 (100 U/ml), Stem Cell Factor (20 ng/ml; Miltenyi Biotec), and TGFbeta1 at 2, 5, or 10 ng/ml (Miltenyi Biotec), while the same medium without TGFbeta1 was used as control. The growth factors were added every third day, and after 3 weeks, the cultures were processed for assessment of surface markers and intracellular cytokine production as described above." || THE CONVERSION STEP IS NOT DATA (Figure 6 legend, verbatim): "As previously reported [24], after exposure to TGFbeta1, the CD56+CD16- subset was significantly enhanced with respect to the CD56+CD16+ subset compared to controls (data not shown). Exposure to TGFbeta1 significantly induced the expression of the proangiogenic cytokines VEGF and PlGF." || RESULTS, verbatim, note the timepoint contradicting the 3-week methods: "In keeping with previous observations [23,24], after 7 days of TGFbeta1 exposure of healthy donor-derived NK cells, a significant increase of the CD56bright CD16- subset (approximately 70% of all NK cells) compared to untreated controls (approximately 30% of NK cells) was observed (data not shown)." || COHORT, verbatim: "NK cells were isolated from blood, lung tumor, and adjacent healthy tissues from 31 NSCLC patients having undergone tumor resection (median age, 71; range, 44-79), as well as blood and macroscopically normal lung tissue from 10 patients having undergone minimal lung resection for bullectomy (median age, 27; range, 16-69)." || AUTHORS' OWN HEDGE, verbatim: "Further studies are needed to fully address whether NK cells from NSCLC patients have other functions and markers of 'bona fide' dNK cells or if they represent a novel NK cell subset." || UPSTREAM Keskin 2007, verbatim (the one real conversion assay in the chain): "To more directly examine the fates of CD16+ and CD16- pNK, the two subsets present in enriched pNK cells were sorted by flow cytometry. After culture in the presence of TGFbeta1, sorted CD16+ pNK cells produced a substantial fraction of CD16- NK cells, whereas the sorted CD16- pNK cells remained relatively unaltered in CD16 expression (Fig. 5)." — but Keskin's own conclusion, verbatim: "Although it is still not possible to draw conclusions on the nature of the in vivo precursor cells of dNK, this study suggests that TGFbeta may play an important role in influencing the dNK phenotype."
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTIVE RECRUITMENT/RETENTION OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET, not conversion — and this alternative is affirmatively supported, not merely unexcluded. (1) Carrega et al., J Immunol 2014 (PMID 24646734) — co-authored by Guido Ferlazzo, who is also a co-author on Bruno 2013 — mapped NK subsets across a wide array of human tissues and found CD56bright-perforin-low non-cytotoxic NK cells are "abundant in BOTH healthy AND neoplastic solid tissues", that subset distribution "appeared in accordance with tissue gene expression of chemotactic factors", and that "chemokine expression pattern of tissues was modified after neoplastic transformation. As a result, although the total amount of NK cells infiltrating the tissues did not significantly change upon malignant transformation, the relative proportion of NK subsets infiltrating the tissues was different." That is a complete, chemokine-mediated recruitment explanation for exactly Bruno's observation, requiring no phenotypic conversion of any cell. (2) The "decidual-like" label is not decidua-specific: CD56bright-perforin-low is the DEFAULT NK phenotype of most healthy human solid tissues, so tumour NK resembling dNK is more parsimoniously "tissue NK resembling tissue NK". Bruno's own contrast is weakened by his controls being ~44 years younger. (3) The in vitro arm cannot discriminate either: starting from BULK NK already ~30% CD56bright-CD16- and ending at ~70% after 3 weeks of IL-2 + SCF + TGF-beta1, with no viability or proliferation accounting and with Keskin having separately noted "fewer cells were recovered from TGFbeta1 cultures", differential survival/expansion of the pre-existing CD56bright fraction fully reproduces the shift. (4) TWO INDEPENDENT ORIGINS, raised by the upstream authors themselves: Keskin 2007 isolated Lin-CD34+CD45+ haematopoietic progenitors from decidua that also generated dNK-like cells, concluding "CD16+ pNK cells or decidual HPC, or both, are possible precursors of dNK cells" — i.e. even in the pregnancy setting the conversion route is one of at least two live hypotheses.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it comes partly from the claim's own author group. PRIMARY COUNTER-EVIDENCE: Carrega P, Bonaccorsi I, Di Carlo E, Morandi B, Paul P, Rizzello V, Cipollone G, Navarra G, Mingari MC, Moretta L, Ferlazzo G. "CD56(bright)perforin(low) noncytotoxic human NK cells are abundant in both healthy and neoplastic solid tissues and recirculate to secondary lymphoid organs via afferent lymph." J Immunol. 2014;192(8):3805-15. PMID 24646734 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_24646734.txt). It proposes and supports a "chemokine switch upon neoplastic transformation" as the mechanism generating the tumour NK subset composition — recruitment, not polarization — and shows the phenotype pre-exists in healthy tissue. SECONDARY: the most recent and most in vivo paper in this lineage, the TGF-betaR1 inhibitor galunisertib PDAC study (Cell Death Dis 2026, PMC13276068), still does not observe conversion: its human data are cross-sectional ("Circulating CD9+ NKs were EXPANDED in PDAC patients" — expansion language, consistent with selection), its polarization data are conditioned-media exposure of healthy-donor PBMC in vitro, and its mouse endpoint is, in its own words, "reduced CD9+ NK cell infiltration" — an abundance/recruitment readout that cannot distinguish blocked conversion from blocked recruitment. Also relevant: Vacca et al., Blood 2008, describes recruitment of circulating NK through decidual tissue as the mechanism of uterine NK accumulation, i.e. the recruitment alternative is the competing account on the decidual side of the analogy too. NO paper found, in any species, using lineage tracing, genetic fate mapping, adoptive transfer, barcoding, or longitudinal paired sampling to show a tumour-associated NK cell acquiring a decidual-like phenotype in vivo.
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY 1: Bruno A, Ferlazzo G, Albini A, Noonan DM. "A think tank of TINK/TANKs: tumor-infiltrating/tumor-associated natural killer cells in tumor progression and angiogenesis." J Natl Cancer Inst. 2014;106(8) (PMID 25178695, PMC4344546) — the framework paper that generalises this claim into the TINK/TANK nomenclature now used across the field; note its own abstract concedes "We SPECULATE on the potential origins of TINKs and TANKs and on the immune signals involved in their differentiation and polarization." CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY 2: Bruno A, Bassani B, Noonan DM, Albini A et al. "Decidual-Like NK Cell Polarization: From Cancer Killing to Cancer Nurturing." Cancer Discov. 2021;11(1):28-33 (PMID 33277305) — an entire perspective whose thesis is that tumour NK are "tricked into dedifferentiating", which presupposes conversion. CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY 3 (therapeutic, and the reason this is HIGH not MEDIUM): the TGF-betaR1 inhibitor galunisertib PDAC study (Cell Death Dis 2026, PMC13276068) uses "limiting decidual-like natural killer cell polarization" as its explicit drug rationale and CD9+ NK frequency as its pharmacodynamic biomarker. If the recruitment alternative is correct, TGF-betaR1 blockade is altering chemokine-driven trafficking rather than reprogramming cells, and CD9+ NK frequency is a trafficking readout mis-specified as a de-polarization readout — which changes the predicted mechanism, the correct dosing/timing window, and the interpretation of the biomarker in any trial built on it. DEPENDENCY 4: the TIMP1/TIMP2 program (Cancers 2021, PMC8507839) is built entirely on the TGF-beta-induced decidual-like polarization assay inheriting the same bulk-culture confound.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's initial call was "INFERENCE (phenotypic similarity)", i.e. INF_MARKER. The audit finds this call DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT BUT ONE RUNG TOO LOW, while the claim's framing is simultaneously too strong. Three separable corrections: (1) UNDERSTATED BY ONE RUNG. The evidence chain is not purely phenotypic-similarity. Bruno 2013 contains an actual in vitro TGF-beta1 perturbation with new data (VEGF/PlGF induction), and the chain's cited upstream, Keskin 2007 PNAS, contains a genuine sorted-population conversion assay in which FACS-purified CD16+CD9- peripheral blood NK gave rise to CD16-CD9+ cells while sorted CD16- controls stayed put — a design that does exclude simple selection WITHIN THAT ASSAY. Strongest class is therefore INF_INVITRO, not INF_MARKER. Per G7 I am not loosening this to make the claim interesting; I am recording that the initial call missed a real in vitro arm. (2) BUT THE TUMOUR-SPECIFIC CLAIM IS ONLY INF_MARKER. The INF_INVITRO ceiling is borrowed from an adjacent, non-tumour, pregnancy-biology paper using healthy-donor blood. Nothing in the tumour literature does the sorted-starting-population experiment. Bruno's own in vitro arm used "Total NK" cells, and — the single most important finding of this audit — the conversion step in Bruno 2013 is not data at all: the CD56bright-CD16- shift is reported twice as "(data not shown)" and attributed to refs [23,24]. The primary source for a "tumour NK BECOMES decidual-like NK" claim contains zero original conversion data. The two "data not shown" passages also contradict each other on timepoint (methods and figure legend say 3 weeks; results say 7 days). (3) THE CLAIM AS WORDED SHOULD BE REWRITTEN. "Tumour NK -> decidual-like NK" asserts a transition. What is actually established is: tumour-infiltrating and tumour-associated NK are enriched for a CD56bright-CD16- pro-angiogenic phenotype that resembles dNK (cross-sectional, age-mismatched controls), and TGF-beta can induce that phenotype in healthy NK in vitro. The arrow is unearned in vivo, and a well-supported competing account (Carrega 2014 chemokine-switch recruitment of a subset that already exists in healthy tissue, from an overlapping author group) is not addressed by any experiment in the chain. Additional hint-verification results: the hint's "Bruno et al. Neoplasia 2013" is CORRECT and is the right primary source (PMID 23441128). The hint's "J Natl Cancer Inst" is a REAL paper but MISATTRIBUTED AS PRIMARY — searched and found: it is Bruno et al., JNCI 2014, PMID 25178695, a REVIEW, disqualified under A.1, and self-described as speculative. The hint's colorectal follow-up is FASEB J 2018 (PMID 29763380), not JNCI. The hint's prediction that "in vitro conversion by TGF-beta/hypoxia would be INF_INVITRO" is confirmed as the operative ceiling; no hypoxia-driven conversion experiment was located for the tumour NK -> dNK-like claim specifically.
audit.notes: CLASSIFICATION LOGIC (G2/G7): no pseudotime or RNA velocity is involved anywhere in this claim, so INF_TRAJECTORY does not arise. OBS_DIRECT/OBS_TRANSFER/OBS_GENETIC are all absent: I searched specifically for lineage tracing, fate mapping, adoptive transfer and longitudinal paired sampling in this literature and found none, in any species. The honest one-line grading is: in vivo tumour component = INF_MARKER; in vitro component = INF_INVITRO (clean only in the non-tumour Keskin assay); overall claim = INF_INVITRO ceiling, INF_MARKER for the tumour-specific assertion. ONE-SENTENCE REWRITE THAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS: "NK cells in NSCLC tumours, adjacent lung and blood are enriched for a CD56bright-CD16- VEGF+/PlGF+ pro-angiogenic phenotype resembling decidual NK, and TGF-beta1 can induce this phenotype in healthy-donor peripheral blood NK in vitro; whether tumour NK are converted or a pre-existing tissue subset is preferentially recruited is unresolved." G5 COMPLIANCE: all n are human subjects, not cells; the in vitro arm's donor n is simply absent from the paper, which is itself a reportable defect. G3 COMPLIANCE: every NOT-FOUND statement above rests on a search actually run and read, listed in searches_run; the only true NOT_SEARCHED areas are non-English literature and preprint servers, which I did not query. ARCHIVED EVIDENCE (absolute paths): /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC3579316_fulltext.txt (Bruno 2013 full text, 60 kB), /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC1805591_fulltext.txt (Keskin 2007 PNAS full text, 44 kB), /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC3579316.txt (lit.py abstract-only record), /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_24646734.txt (Carrega 2014 counter-evidence record). TOOLING NOTE FOR THE SCREEN: `lit.py methods` silently degrades to STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY for PMC records outside the OA subset (EuropePMC fullTextXML 404s). Bruno 2013 is exactly such a record. Any row in this screen graded off lit.py output alone for a non-OA PMC article will have been graded off an abstract — which for this claim would have produced the opposite conclusion, since Bruno's abstract asserts TGF-beta1 "upregulated VEGF and PlGF" and reads as though polarization were shown, whereas the full text marks the phenotype switch "(data not shown)". This is a textbook G1 case and other rows should be re-checked for the same failure mode.

adv.challenge_reason:
DOWNGRADE INF_INVITRO -> INF_MARKER for claim X3 as scoped ("TUMOUR NK -> decidual-like/pro-angiogenic NK").

I re-ran `lit.py methods 23441128 --tag X3` myself: it returns STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY (PMC3579316 is outside the OA subset), so I independently re-extracted the raw PMC HTML and re-verified every quote in the row rather than inheriting them. The prior auditor's verbatim quotes are ACCURATE. Three of their factual findings are UPHELD on my own reading: (i) the conversion step is "(data not shown)" in BOTH the Results and the Fig 6 legend and is attributed to refs [23,24]; (ii) the timepoint is internally contradictory (Methods and Fig 6 legend say "after 3 weeks", Results says "after 7 days"); (iii) the in vitro arm is bulk "Total NK cells", with no donor n, no "n =" statement anywhere.

WHERE I OVERTURN THEM. The upgrade to INF_INVITRO is a DOUBLE-COUNT of a different claim's evidence, and it is not licensed by the primary source.

(1) KESKIN IS ALREADY ANOTHER CLAIM'S PRIMARY SOURCE. /home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC1805591.txt exists (header: "# status=ABSTRACT_ONLY pmid=17360654 pmcid=PMC1805591"), i.e. Keskin 2007 is this screen's primary source for claim D3. Borrowing D3's sorted-conversion assay to set X3's ceiling grades X3 on evidence for a different arrow. The prereg (docs/PREREGISTRATION.md line 38) assigns each claim exactly one strongest class on its own evidence.

(2) THE BORROWED ASSAY HAS THE WRONG "A". Keskin's A is healthy-donor PERIPHERAL BLOOD NK and its inducer is decidual stromal conditioned medium / TGF-beta1 in a pregnancy setting. No tumour, no tumour-derived factor, no cancer patient. It cannot supply the class for a tumour-NK arrow.

(3) BRUNO'S OWN IN VITRO ARM ALSO HAS THE WRONG "A" AND THE WRONG ENDPOINT. Verified verbatim from Methods: the cultured cells are "peripheral blood NK cells isolated from buffy coats of HEALTHY DONORS". Tumour NK are never cultured anywhere in the paper. And the measured endpoint is intracellular VEGF/PlGF WITHIN a CD56+CD16- GATE — cytokine content inside a pre-defined gate cannot establish that any cell entered that gate. The only statement about entering the gate is "(data not shown)". So the primary source contains no original data of A being cultured into B; INF_INVITRO ("A cultured into a B-like phenotype in vitro") is not met by X3's own primary source.

WHERE THE PRIOR AUDIT UNDERSTATED THE EVIDENCE (recorded for honesty, G7 both directions). Keskin's assay is materially STRONGER than the row credits, and the row's alternative-explanation point (3) partly misfires against it: I read Keskin's raw text and it states the sort was "very high purity (i.e., the contamination with CD16- pNK cells was <0.1%)", that CFSE labelling was performed, and that the transition "was accompanied by cell division, although not at levels sufficient to suggest outgrowth of very rare cells", over a 2-week incubation. That design does exclude simple selective outgrowth within that assay — but it remains D3's evidence, in a non-tumour system, so it does not rescue X3.

NET: no OBS_* class was wrongly credited (the row correctly found no fate mapping, transfer or barcoding, and I independently confirmed none exists for this claim). No trajectory inference is involved, so G2 does not arise. The error is the opposite of the usual one: a genuine in vitro conversion assay was imported from an adjacent claim to raise a claim whose own primary source is pure cross-sectional marker similarity.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest:
INF_MARKER

evidence_types_all present for X3: INF_MARKER (dominant and load-bearing: cross-sectional flow-cytometric phenotype similarity between NSCLC-infiltrating NK and published dNK markers, in 31 patients at a single surgical timepoint) + a weak INF_INVITRO fragment that supports only the sub-proposition "TGF-beta1 raises intracellular VEGF/PlGF staining in bulk healthy-donor NK cultures", NOT the arrow. INF_INVITRO for the arrow itself exists only in adjacent claims whose A is peripheral blood NK (Keskin 2007 PMID 17360654 = claim D3; Cerdeira 2013 PMID 23487420), not tumour NK. NOT present: OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER, OBS_GENETIC, INF_TRAJECTORY, INF_KINETIC (the paper has no time course at all — its one timepoint statement is self-contradictory, 3 weeks vs 7 days).
adv.new_counter_evidence:
The prior audit reported counter_evidence=FOUND but MISSED the single most damaging item: a named FAILED REPLICATION of the primary source's core readout.

(A) HAWKE LG, WHITFORD MKM, ORMISTON ML. "The Production of Pro-angiogenic VEGF-A Isoforms by Hypoxic Human NK Cells Is Independent of Their TGF-beta-Mediated Conversion to an ILC1-Like Phenotype." Front Immunol. 2020;11:1903. PMID 32983113 / PMC7477355. Full text retrieved and archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC7477355_fulltext.txt. I verified from Hawke's own reference list that their ref (10) IS Bruno 2013. Four separate blows:
  - FAILED REPLICATION, verbatim: "Even long-term exposure of circulating NK cells to TGF-beta for 7-21 days failed to induce measurable VEGF-A secretion, contrasting with previous reports that used intracellular flow cytometry to quantify VEGF-A production (10)."
  - TECHNICAL ARTEFACT allegation against Bruno's exact assay, verbatim: "the use of FISH-flow cytometry for this purpose was necessitated by the failure of multiple antibodies to detect VEGF-A using standard intracellular staining protocols. This result, which contrasts with other publications that used the same anti-VEGF-A antibodies for this purpose (10, 21-24), highlights the need for robust positive and negative controls in such assays." Bruno's ENTIRE human and in vitro readout is intracellular anti-VEGF-A/PlGF flow cytometry, with no isotype/positive/negative control reported.
  - CAUSAL DISSOCIATION (destroys Bruno's thesis): TGF-beta drives CD9/CD103 acquisition; hypoxia drives VEGFA; they are independent. Verbatim: "Co-staining of VEGFA mRNA with CD9 and CD103 in hypoxic NK cells revealed no enrichment of VEGFA gene expression in the subset of NK cells that adopt an ILC1-like phenotype in response to TGF-beta vs. those that did not". And: "These findings argue against the suggestion that TGF-beta and hypoxia act in concert to promote the conversion of circulating NK cells to an angiogenic dNK-like phenotype." So "decidual-like polarization" is not what makes NK pro-angiogenic.
  - "BECOMES" IS THE WRONG VERB: "VEGF-A production by circulating NK cells is a transient phenomenon, which can be reversed upon returning hypoxic NK cells to a normoxic environment... bidirectional and is not associated with a permanent change in cellular function." n = 3 healthy donors.

(B) SOJKA DK et al. eLife 2014;3:e01659. PMID 24714492 / PMC3975579 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_PMC3975579_fulltext.txt). PARABIOSIS + transcription-factor-deficient and athymic nude mice. Verbatim: "there are at least four distinct lineages of NK cells: cNK, thymic, liver (and skin) trNK, and uterine trNK cells." Uterine NK are a DISTINCT, NON-RECIRCULATING TISSUE-RESIDENT LINEAGE. This is the TWO-INDEPENDENT-ORIGINS alternative established at the strongest available methodological tier, and it attacks the REFERENCE POLE of the analogy: if uNK are not converted circulating NK, then "tumour NK becomes decidual-like NK" likens a tumour cell to a cell type that is itself a separate lineage.

(C) GAO Y et al. "Tumor immunoevasion by the conversion of effector NK cells into type 1 innate lymphoid cells." Nat Immunol. 2017;18:1004-15. PMID 28759001. Genetically engineered mouse models. The SAME TGF-beta axis, in the SAME setting (tumour), interrogated with the strong method, names the destination ILC1/intILC1 — NOT "decidual-like NK". The strong experiment HAS been done on this mechanism and it did not produce X3's answer. CAVEAT (G3): a 2024 Author Correction exists (Nat Immunol s41590-024-01799-9) concerning data in specific figures, main conclusion stated unaffected; I did NOT read the correction in full.

(D) CERDEIRA AS et al. "Conversion of peripheral blood NK cells to a decidual NK-like phenotype by a cocktail of defined factors." J Immunol. 2013;190(8):3939-48. PMID 23487420. The prior audit stated "no hypoxia-driven conversion experiment was located" — IT EXISTS and I found it. It cuts against the claim: dNK markers required hypoxia + TGF-beta1 + a DEMETHYLATING AGENT, i.e. global pharmacological demethylation, arguing the route is not physiological. (Methods not retrieved in full — abstract-level only.)

(E) CD16-SHEDDING ARTEFACT (never raised by the prior audit). CD16 loss on NK is ADAM17-mediated proteolytic shedding on activation (Romee et al., Blood 2013;121(18):3599; Blood 2011;118(21):2184). The CD16+ -> CD16- "transition" anchoring the whole chain can be receptor cleavage on an unchanged cell. Keskin partially guards against this (CD9 co-acquired, CD94 stable) but neither Keskin nor Bruno used an ADAM17 inhibitor. CAVEAT (G3): established from search-result summaries of the Blood records; I did NOT fetch Romee full text.

(F) CARREGA P et al. Cancer 2008;112:863-75. PMID 18203207. The CD56bright CD16- enrichment in NSCLC was published FIVE YEARS before Bruno with no conversion claim; Bruno's own Results opens "Previous studies have shown that tumor samples from patients with NSCLC are enriched in the CD56+CD16- NK subset". Enrichment is the datum; conversion is an overlay added later.

(G) UNEXAMINED CO-LOAD-BEARING UPSTREAM. Bruno attributes the "data not shown" phenotype switch to refs [23,24]. Ref 24 is Keskin. Ref 23 — never named by the prior audit — is ALLAN DS et al., "TGF-beta affects DEVELOPMENT AND DIFFERENTIATION of human natural killer cell subsets", Eur J Immunol 2010;40:2289-95, PMID 20540115 / PMC3066635 (I resolved this from Bruno's own reference list and confirmed via NCBI esummary). Its title points at progenitor development, a DIFFERENT mechanism from mature-cell conversion. Methods NOT retrieved this round — flagged for follow-up.

Also note an ambiguity the prior audit missed: Bruno's "7 days" sentence begins "In keeping with previous observations [23,24], after 7 days of TGFbeta1 exposure..." — so it is undecidable whether Bruno is reporting his own unshown 7-day data or restating refs 23/24. The reader cannot tell whose experiment the phenotype switch even is.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The home fields have already answered this structural question, with methods nobody has applied to X3.

1. TRM / RECRUITMENT-vs-RESIDENCY (the field that owns this question). Definitive residency assignment requires parabiosis (mouse) or transplant/sex-mismatch chimerism (human); marker phenotype cannot do it. The reason is fatal to X3's specific markers: TGF-beta induces CD9/CD103/CD49a on ANY lymphocyte entering tissue. Hawke 2020 states this explicitly, verbatim: "TGF-beta, in combination with other factors like IL-15, induce the expression of vital integrins, like CD9 and CD103, not only on NK cells, but also on other lymphocyte subsets like resident memory T cells... Such changes are essential to the migration and retention of these lymphocyte subsets into tissues." CONSEQUENCE: CD56bright/CD16-lo/CD9+/CD103+/CD49a+ is a GENERIC TGF-beta TISSUE-ENTRY SIGNATURE shared with CD8 TRM, not a decidua-specific identity. "Decidual-like" is a misnaming of "tissue-entry-like" — which is exactly what Bruno's own hedge concedes: "Further studies are needed to fully address whether NK cells from NSCLC patients have other functions and markers of 'bona fide' dNK cells or if they represent a novel NK cell subset." Sojka 2014 (PMID 24714492) applied the parabiosis standard inside the NK lineage and got FOUR SEPARATE LINEAGES, including a distinct uterine trNK lineage. Human lung transplant chimerism (Snyder et al., Sci Immunol 2019) is the available human method; searched — never applied to tumour NK "decidualization".

2. MYELOID / ANGIOGENIC REPROGRAMMING (the closest structural analogue: a pro-angiogenic tumour-associated phenotype). Three findings, all against X3:
 - Murray PJ et al., Immunity 2014;41:14-20, PMID 25035950. Formal consensus nomenclature and experimental guidelines, written precisely because in vitro polarization states do NOT map onto in vivo tumour-associated cells and because marker panels were being read as identities. It mandates reporting the macrophage SOURCE, the ACTIVATOR, and a defined marker set. Bruno 2013 fails all three in its in vitro arm (bulk unsorted "Total NK" source, no donor n, no defined marker panel for the unshown switch). X3 is a textbook repetition of the M1/M2 error the myeloid field formally repudiated.
 - Loyher PL et al., "Macrophages of distinct origins contribute to tumor development in the lung", J Exp Med 2018, PMID 30201786. FATE MAPPING showed lung TAMs have TWO origins — embryonic tissue-resident macrophages expanding in situ PLUS recruited monocyte-derived cells. Marker phenotyping had never resolved this; only lineage tracing did, and the answer was two origins, not conversion.
 - De Palma M et al., Cancer Cell 2005;8:211-26, PMID 16169466. TIE2-expressing monocytes are a PRE-EXISTING, SEPARATELY RECRUITED proangiogenic lineage; TEM elimination did not change total TAM numbers, so TEMs are not merely converted TAM precursors. This is the canonical A.4 alternative — "a pre-existing subset was selected, not converted" — already PROVEN for a pro-angiogenic tumour myeloid population. X3 asserts the converse for a pro-angiogenic tumour lymphoid population using strictly weaker evidence.

3. EXHAUSTION / EXPORTED FUNCTIONAL LABELS. Blank CU et al., "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'", Nat Rev Immunol 2019;19:665-674, PMID 31570879 — it took an 18-expert consensus to define the term even in CD8 T cells, and the panel did not converge on a single definition. The NK field has no equivalent consensus and the literature warns that exhaustion, anergy, senescence and suppression are routinely conflated in NK (Front Cell Infect Microbiol 2020, PMC7031155; Roe, Immunology 2022, PMID 35266556). BEARING: "decidual-like polarization" is an exported functional label with even less definitional discipline than "NK exhaustion" — a borrowed name doing the work of a mechanism.

4. ILC FIELD. Gao 2017 (PMID 28759001) is the ILC field's answer to the identical stimulus in the identical setting: genetically engineered mice, TGF-beta-dependent NK -> intILC1/ILC1 in tumours. Same input, stronger method, DIFFERENT named destination. Hawke 2020 independently calls the human TGF-beta product "ILC1-like", not "decidual-like". Two independent groups converge on ILC1; only the Bruno/Albini/Noonan group calls it decidual.

CONVERGENT VERDICT: every home field that possesses the discriminating method (parabiosis, chimerism, fate mapping) has applied it to its own version of this question, and in every case the answer was either TWO ORIGINS or SELECTIVE RECRUITMENT OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET — never the marker-similarity conversion that X3 asserts.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
The prior audit set HIGH, resting that call almost entirely on the therapeutic dependency (galunisertib PDAC study). I downgrade to MEDIUM on two grounds.

(1) THE THERAPEUTIC DEPENDENCY IS NOT ACTUALLY LOAD-BEARING ON X3. TGF-betaR1 blockade in tumours is independently and far better motivated by (a) Gao 2017 (PMID 28759001), TGF-beta-dependent NK -> ILC1 conversion demonstrated in genetically engineered mice, and (b) TGF-beta's direct suppression of NKG2D and NK cytotoxicity, which Bruno himself cites (Lee et al., J Immunol 2004, PMID 15187109). If the "decidual-like polarization" framing were deleted tomorrow, the drug rationale would survive untouched on either of those. A claim sitting decoratively on top of an independently justified target is not load-bearing at HIGH. Additionally, per G3 I must record that I did NOT independently retrieve that paper this round — the prior audit gave only "PMC13276068" with no PMID and I did not fetch it — so the row's strongest HIGH argument is also its least verified one.

(2) THE OTHER NAMED DEPENDENCIES ARE REVIEWS AND PERSPECTIVES, WHICH PROPAGATE FRAMING, NOT EXPERIMENTAL PROGRAMS. Bruno et al. JNCI 2014 (PMID 25178695) is a review that self-describes as speculative ("We SPECULATE on the potential origins of TINKs and TANKs"); Cancer Discov 2021 (PMID 33277305) is a perspective. If X3 falls, these need rewording, not retraction. Crucially, the underlying observation is INDEPENDENT of the claim and survives it: Carrega et al. Cancer 2008 (PMID 18203207) established CD56bright CD16- enrichment in NSCLC five years earlier with no conversion claim attached. So nothing experimental collapses.

WHY NOT LOW. Two concrete dependencies are real and testable, so this is not LOW:
 - NAMED DEPENDENCY 1 (nomenclature): Bruno A, Ferlazzo G, Albini A, Noonan DM, "A think tank of TINK/TANKs...", J Natl Cancer Inst 2014;106(8), PMID 25178695. The TINK/TANK vocabulary and the "decidual-like NK polarization" frame (Cancer Discov 2021, PMID 33277305) are now field-standard terms that presuppose the arrow. Any downstream study inheriting the word "polarization" inherits an unearned causal claim.
 - NAMED DEPENDENCY 2 (measurement, and the sharpest one — newly identified this round): every study that uses INTRACELLULAR ANTI-VEGF-A FLOW CYTOMETRY IN NK CELLS as its readout inherits Bruno's assay, and Hawke et al. 2020 (PMID 32983113) report that multiple antibodies — "the same anti-VEGF-A antibodies" — failed to detect VEGF-A in NK cells under standard intracellular protocols, forcing them to FISH-flow. This is a concrete, falsifiable, method-level dependency that propagates to every paper in the chain including the TIMP1/TIMP2 program, and it is independent of whether the conversion claim is true.

MEDIUM is the honest call: substantial vocabulary and assay-level propagation, no experimental program that fails if the arrow is wrong.
adv.better_primary_source:
Bruno 2013 (PMID 23441128 / PMC3579316) is UPHELD as X3's primary source — it is the first paper to attach the decidual analogy to tumour NK, it is not a review, and full text is obtainable (though only outside the standard route; lit.py degrades to ABSTRACT_ONLY, which I reconfirmed myself). Three corrections to how the row sources X3:

(1) DO NOT USE KESKIN 2007 (PMID 17360654 / PMC1805591) AS X3's SOURCE. It is already this screen's primary source for claim D3 (/home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC1805591.txt). Using it for X3 double-counts one assay across two claims and imports a pregnancy-biology, healthy-blood-NK arrow into a tumour claim.

(2) THE TRUE ORIGINAL FOR THE PHENOTYPE OBSERVATION IS EARLIER AND MAKES NO CONVERSION CLAIM: Carrega P, Morandi B, Costa R, Frumento G, Forte G, Altavilla G, Ratto GB, Mingari MC, Moretta L, Ferlazzo G. "Natural killer cells infiltrating human nonsmall-cell lung cancer are enriched in CD56 bright CD16(-) cells and display an impaired capability to kill tumor cells." Cancer. 2008;112:863-875. PMID 18203207. Bruno cites it as ref 17 and opens his Results with it. The row should record that the datum (enrichment) predates the claim (conversion) by five years and is separable from it — which is itself evidence that the arrow is an interpretive overlay.

(3) AN UNEXAMINED CO-LOAD-BEARING UPSTREAM MUST BE ADDED AND CHECKED. Bruno attributes the "(data not shown)" phenotype switch to refs [23,24]. The prior audit chased only ref 24 (Keskin) and never named ref 23: ALLAN DS, RYBALOV B, AWONG G, ZUNIGA-PFLUCKER JC, KOPCOW HD, CARLYLE JR, STROMINGER JL. "TGF-beta affects development and differentiation of human natural killer cell subsets." Eur J Immunol. 2010;40:2289-2295. PMID 20540115 / PMC3066635 (resolved from Bruno's reference list and confirmed by NCBI esummary). Its title indicates DEVELOPMENT/DIFFERENTIATION — plausibly a progenitor route, a mechanistically DIFFERENT proposition from mature-cell conversion. I did NOT retrieve its methods this round (NOT_SEARCHED at methods level); it should be pulled before X3 is finalised, because half of the citation load for the claim's only conversion statement rests on it.

REQUIRED ADDITIONS TO THE ROW'S EVIDENCE SET (counter-evidence, all newly found this round): Hawke 2020 PMID 32983113 (failed replication + causal dissociation + reversibility); Sojka 2014 PMID 24714492 (parabiosis, four distinct NK lineages incl. uterine trNK); Gao 2017 PMID 28759001 (same axis, stronger method, destination = ILC1); Cerdeira 2013 PMID 23487420 (the hypoxia conversion paper the prior audit reported as not located — it exists).

SUGGESTED REWRITE, tighter than the prior audit's: "NK cells in NSCLC tumours are enriched for a CD56bright CD16- phenotype (already reported by Carrega 2008), and Bruno 2013 additionally reports intracellular VEGF/PlGF staining in that gate at one cross-sectional timepoint with ~44-year-younger controls. The paper contains no original data on conversion — the phenotype switch is 'data not shown' and attributed to refs 23/24 — and a later group could not detect VEGF-A in NK cells with the same antibodies. Whether tumour NK convert, whether a pre-existing tissue-resident subset is recruited, and whether the destination is better described as ILC1-like than decidual-like, are all unresolved."
